fr_passeport_noun.hook: A girl in a yellow raincoat shows her PASSPORT at the window while the rain POURS down: PASS, POUR! pahs-POR.
fr_passeport_noun.why: Duck in a raincoat replaced by a human girl (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_rendez_vous_noun.hook: A boy with a bouquet checks his pocket watch: his RENDEZVOUS is late! English borrowed the same word: rahn-day-VOO.
fr_rendez_vous_noun.why: Hedgehog replaced by a human boy (no anthropomorphic animal that is not the hook).

fr_ficelle_noun.hook: TWINE is wound round the neck of a CELLO: fee-SEHL = fi-CELL(o)!
fr_ficelle_noun.why: Old hook described a shop-mouse that is not painted; the painted cello with twine is now the hook.

fr_stylo_noun.hook: A STYLISH PEN in a pink scarf leans on the desk, striking a pose: STY-LO! stee-LOH.
fr_stylo_noun.why: Desk zoom re-cut from the town hall painting; the pen there wears a pink scarf (its sunglasses are too small to see), so the hook names only what is visible.

fr_feuille_noun_2.hook: This SHEET of writing paper is cut in the shape of a LEAF, because French uses one word for both: une feuille (de papier).
fr_feuille_noun_2.why: RECS 1.4: paper sense split from the leaf (fr_feuille_noun, foret/arbres).
